names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 28 Μαΐου, «Άγιος Ανδρέας ο διά Χριστόν σαλός», with the rank word left off. The epithet «ο διά Χριστόν σαλός» is left off with the rank.
The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 180, «Андрей Константинопольский, Христа ради юродивый», with the epithet left to the display name.

death.note: The year the Russian calendar prints after his name, «Блж. Андрея, Христа ради юродивого (936)». The folder held no date at all before this reading; saint.gr places him by the reign of Constantine VII Porphyrogennetos instead.

feast.note: The Greek keeps him on 28 May and the Russian on 2 October, two days for one man. The Russian day is the eve of the Protection of the Mother of God, which is his vision in the church at Blachernae, and that is why it sits where it does.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, 2 октября ст. ст. — «Блж. Андрея, Христа ради юродивого (936).»
source.note: The rank is the alt text of the icon the page sets before the group of lines this one stands in, «Cовершается служба, не отмеченная в Типиконе никаким знаком» — a service the Typikon marks with no sign at all.

attestations.note: The Russian gives the year the Greek page does not: 936. It also marks him «блж.», blessed, where the Greek has ὅσιος.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 28ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Ανδρέας ο διά Χριστόν σαλός»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 28 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The page places the vision of the Mother of God at the Blachernae in the same breath as the feast of the Protection — «είδε τη Θεοτόκο στον ουρανό προσευχόμενη και σκέπουσα το λαό με το τίμιο ωμοφόριό της ( 1 και 28 Οκτωβρίου)» — so it points at two October days as well, but those are the feast of the Protection and not a second commemoration of him, and no second row or folder is made on that account. The page gives no year of birth and no year of death, only the reign it sets him in, so there is no `dates` object here. It prints an apolytikion, two kontakia, a megalynarion, an oikos and a kathisma; the apolytikion is taken.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026).
